units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 2. The state service management body is established for the purposes of:
units.label: Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 1) developing proposals for personnel policy in state bodies of the City of Moscow and monitoring its implementation;
units.label: Point 1 Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 2) coordinating the activities of state bodies in matters of entry into civil service, formation of the personnel reserve, performance and termination of civil service, use of the personnel reserve, and training and professional education of civil servants, and monitoring state bodies’ compliance with civil service legislation.
units.label: Point 2 Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 3) preparing and submitting, in the prescribed manner, proposals for implementing civil service legislation;
units.label: Point 3 Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 4) supporting the work of the conflict-of-interest resolution commission established in the state service management body, participating in the work of analogous commissions established in state bodies, and participating in commissions conducting competitions to fill civil service positions and appraisals of civil servants;
units.label: Point 4 Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 5) determining periods of service (work) included in length of civil service;
units.label: Point 5 Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 56. State service management body
units.text: 6) preparing explanations and recommendations for state bodies on civil service matters.
units.label: Point 6 Part 2 Art. 56

units.locator: Article 57. Liability for violations of civil service legislation
units.text: Article 57. Liability for violations of civil service legislation
units.label: Art. 57

units.locator: Article 57. Liability for violations of civil service legislation
units.text: Persons responsible for violating the legislation of the Russian Federation on the state civil service of the Russian Federation are held liable in accordance with the procedure established by federal laws.
units.label: Art. 57 · text

units.locator: Chapter 15. Consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: Chapter 15. Consideration of individual service disputes
units.label: Chapter 15. Consideration of individual service disputes

units.locator: Article 58. Individual service dispute
units.text: Article 58. Individual service dispute
units.label: Art. 58

units.locator: Article 58. Individual service dispute
units.text: An individual service dispute means unresolved disagreements between the employer's representative and a civil servant, or a citizen entering or formerly in civil service, concerning the application of laws, other regulatory legal acts on civil service or the service contract, which have been submitted to a body for consideration of individual service disputes.
units.label: Art. 58 · text

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.label: Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 1. Individual service disputes (hereinafter service disputes) shall be considered by the following bodies for consideration of individual service disputes (hereinafter service dispute bodies):
units.label: Part 1 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 1) the service disputes commission; 2) a court.
units.label: Point 1 Part 1 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 2. The procedure for considering service disputes in service dispute bodies is regulated by federal laws.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 3. A service disputes commission is established by decision of the employer’s representative and consists of equal numbers of representatives appointed by the employer’s representative and civil servants’ representatives elected at a meeting (conference) of the state body’s civil servants, including a representative (representatives) of that state body’s elected trade union body (bodies).
units.label: Part 3 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 4. A meeting (conference) of the state body’s civil servants is held by decision of the employer’s representative, including in response to an application by civil servants or the state body’s elected trade union body. The procedure for holding the meeting (conference) and for the civil servants’ adoption of decisions is regulated by federal law.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 5. The service disputes commission shall have its own seal. Organizational and technical support for its activities shall be provided by the state body.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 6. A model regulation on the service disputes commission is approved by a decree of the Mayor of Moscow on the proposal of the state service management body.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 7. The service disputes commission shall elect a chairperson and secretary from among its members.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 8. A service dispute shall be considered by the service disputes commission if the civil servant, acting independently or with a representative, has not resolved the disagreements through direct negotiations with the employer's representative.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 9. A civil servant, or a citizen entering or formerly in civil service, may apply to the service disputes commission within three months from the day on which they learned or should have learned that their right had been violated.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 10. If the period established by part 9 of this Article is missed for valid reasons, the service disputes commission may restore that period and consider the merits of the service dispute. A written application received from a civil servant or a citizen entering or formerly in the civil service must be registered by the commission on the day it is submitted.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 11. The service disputes commission must consider a service dispute within 10 calendar days from submission of the written application by a civil servant or a citizen entering or formerly in the civil service.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 59

units.locator: Article 59. Bodies for the consideration of individual service disputes
units.text: 12. The procedure for consideration of a service dispute by the service disputes commission is regulated by federal law.
units.label: Part 12 Art. 59

units.locator: Chapter 16. Final and transitional provisions
units.text: Chapter 16. Final and transitional provisions
units.label: Chapter 16. Final and transitional provisions

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.label: Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 1. This Law enters into force on 1 February 2005, except for part 8 of Article 6; point 2 of part 1 of Article 10 (insofar as it concerns familiarization with criteria for assessing the efficiency of performance of official duties and performance indicators for professional service activities); point 17 of part 1 of Article 10; point 4 of part 1 of Article 12; point 8 of part 2 of Article 20 (insofar as it concerns types and conditions of medical insurance); point 4 of part 3 of Article 20; Articles 36, 39 and 40; point 9 of part 1 of Article 42; and part 3 of Article 43.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 2. Part 8 of Article 6 of this Law enters into force after a federal law or decree of the President of the Russian Federation determines the correspondence between federal state civil service positions and standard state civil service positions of constituent entities of the Russian Federation.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 3. Point 2 of part 1 of Article 10 (insofar as it concerns familiarization with criteria for assessing the efficiency of performance of official duties and performance indicators for professional service activities), point 4 of part 3 of Article 20, and point 8 of part 2 of Article 36 of this Law enter into force after the President of the Russian Federation and the Government of the Russian Federation respectively approve general indicators, common to state bodies and civil servants, of the efficiency and effectiveness of state bodies’ activities, the adoption and implementation of managerial and other decisions, and the legal, organizational and documentary support for implementation of those decisions.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 4. Point 17 of part 1 of Article 10 and point 8 of part 2 of Article 20 of this Law (insofar as the latter concerns types and conditions of medical insurance) enter into force after the federal law on medical insurance for state servants of the Russian Federation enters into force.
units.label: Part 4 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 5. Point 4 of part 1 of Article 12 of this Law enters into force after the authorized federal executive authority establishes the procedure for medical examinations, the list of diseases preventing entry into or performance of the civil service, and the form of the medical conclusion.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 6. This part was repealed with effect from 17 October 2009 by Law of the City of Moscow of 16 September 2009 No. 34.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 7. Article 36 of this Law enters into force after the administrative regulations of the relevant state bodies are approved by acts of those bodies. The administrative regulations of the Staff Office of the Moscow City Duma are approved by an act of the Head of that Staff Office.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 8. The provisions of Articles 39 and 40 of this Law enter into force in relation to civil servants after the relevant decrees of the Mayor of Moscow enter into force.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 9. Point 9 of part 1 of Article 42 of this Law enters into force in relation to civil servants after the relevant decree of the Mayor of Moscow enters into force.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 10. Part 3 of Article 43 of this Law enters into force on the date of entry into force of the federal law on state pension provision for citizens of the Russian Federation who have performed state service and their families.
units.label: Part 10 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 60. Entry into force of this Law
units.text: 11. Laws and regulatory legal acts of the City of Moscow regulating the procedure and conditions for entry into, performance of and termination of the state service of the City of Moscow apply insofar as they do not conflict with civil service legislation.
units.label: Part 11 Art. 60

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.label: Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 1. Until the relevant decree of the Mayor of Moscow enters into force, a citizen entering the civil service and a civil servant submit information on income received, property owned that is subject to taxation, and property-related obligations using the form established for federal state civil servants. A copy of the income declaration is also submitted to the state body’s structural subdivision for state service and personnel matters.
units.label: Part 1 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 2. The monetary remuneration payment conditions in force on the date this Law enters into force for state servants of the City of Moscow recognized as civil servants under this Law — including position salary amounts, established allowances and their payment conditions and procedure, and the procedure, conditions and amounts of additional state guarantees — remain applicable until the decrees of the Mayor of Moscow establishing civil servants’ monetary remuneration in accordance with this Law enter into force.
units.label: Part 2 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 3. The amount of monetary remuneration established for civil servants under this Law may not be less than the amount established for state servants on the date this Law enters into force.
units.label: Part 3 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 4. State servants of the City of Moscow recognized as civil servants under this Law are conferred the following class ranks by an act of the state body:
units.label: Part 4 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 1) holders of the class rank of the state service of the City of Moscow of the 1st, 2nd or 3rd class — Active State Councillor of the City of Moscow, 1st, 2nd or 3rd class, respectively;
units.label: Point 1 Part 4 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 2) holders of the class rank of the state service of the City of Moscow of the 4th, 5th or 6th class — State Councillor of the City of Moscow, 1st, 2nd or 3rd class, respectively;
units.label: Point 2 Part 4 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 3) holders of the class rank of the state service of the City of Moscow of the 7th, 8th or 9th class — State Civil Service Councillor of the City of Moscow, 1st, 2nd or 3rd class, respectively; 4) holders of the class rank of the state service of the City of Moscow of the 10th, 11th or 12th class — State Civil Service Referent of the City of Moscow, 1st, 2nd or 3rd class, respectively;
units.label: Point 3 Part 4 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 5) holders of the class rank of the state service of the City of Moscow of the 13th, 14th or 15th class — State Civil Service Secretary of the City of Moscow, 1st, 2nd or 3rd class, respectively.
units.label: Point 5 Part 4 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 5. Periods of work (service) previously included (credited), in accordance with the established procedure, in length of state service are credited towards length of civil service for monthly allowances to the position salary for length of civil service, additional annual paid leave for length of service, civil service incentives, pension supplements and other calculations of length of civil service under this Law.
units.label: Part 5 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 6. Until the federal law on medical insurance for state servants of the Russian Federation enters into force, civil servants and their family members, including after the civil servants retire on a length-of-service pension, including state servants recognized as civil servants under this Law, and retired state servants entitled to medical and sanatorium or health-resort services, retain the conditions of sanatorium or health-resort services and receive compensation for medical care in accordance with the procedure and conditions provided for by the relevant decree of the Mayor of Moscow.
units.label: Part 6 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 7. The procedure and conditions for establishing supplements to length-of-service pensions for civil servants and state servants recognized as civil servants under this Law are retained until the federal law on state pension provision for citizens of the Russian Federation who have performed state service and their families enters into force.
units.label: Part 7 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 8. Until the state service management body provided for by Article 56 of this Law is established, its tasks and functions are performed by the Staff Office of the Mayor and Government of Moscow.
units.label: Part 8 Art. 61

units.locator: Article 61. Transitional provisions
units.text: 9. Provisions of this Law’s articles referring to relevant federal regulatory legal acts apply, until those acts enter into force, in accordance with the procedure established by this Law and the relevant decrees of the Mayor of Moscow.
units.label: Part 9 Art. 61

units.text: Article 62. Repeal of certain laws of the City of Moscow

units.text: 1) Law of the City of Moscow of 29 October 1997 No. 43 ‘On the State Service of the City of Moscow’;

units.text: 2) Law of the City of Moscow of 13 September 2000 No. 29 ‘On Incentives for State Servants of the City of Moscow’.
units.label: Point 2 Art. 62

units.locator: Article 63. Bringing regulatory legal acts of the City of Moscow on state service into conformity with this Law
units.text: Article 63. Bringing regulatory legal acts of the City of Moscow on state service into conformity with this Law
units.label: Art. 63

units.locator: Article 63. Bringing regulatory legal acts of the City of Moscow on state service into conformity with this Law
units.text: The Mayor of Moscow and the Government of Moscow are invited to bring regulatory legal acts of the City of Moscow on state service into conformity with this Law within six months of its entry into force.
units.label: Art. 63 · “The Mayor of Moscow and the Government of Moscow are invited to…”

units.locator: Article 63. Bringing regulatory legal acts of the City of Moscow on state service into conformity with this Law
units.text: Mayor of Moscow Yu. M. Luzhkov
units.label: Art. 63 · “Mayor of Moscow Yu. M. Luzhkov”
